independentDerivations.derivation: Orient each parallel branch from node A to B. U_i=V_A-V_B=U and q_i=C_i*U. Charge on node A is q=sum(q_i)=U*sum(C_i), hence C_parallel=sum(C_i). For n>=2 and every C_i>0, C_parallel-C_k=sum(i!=k,C_i)>0.
independentDerivations.conclusion: Shared nodes, not positive/negative charge labels, define parallel. The inequality excludes the one-capacitor boundary.

independentDerivations.derivation: Orient consecutive capacitors left to right with left charge q_i and right charge -q_i. Floating intermediate node i has net charge -q_i+q_(i+1). Its individually zero initial charge and isolation give q_(i+1)=q_i=q. Telescoping voltages yield U=sum(q/C_i), so 1/C_series=sum(1/C_i). For n>=2 and all positive C_i, 1/C_series>1/C_k, hence C_series<C_k.
independentDerivations.conclusion: The written neutrality condition is interpreted per intermediate conductor group, not merely as zero aggregate charge over the whole chain.

independentDerivations.derivation: If a middle node instead has conserved charge Q0, then -q_i+q_(i+1)=Q0 and adjacent capacitor charges need not match. The incremental series capacitance can remain the reciprocal sum, but an absolute charge/voltage ratio has an offset. For neutral series capacitors U_i=q/C_i, so unequal C_i give unequal voltage divisions.
independentDerivations.conclusion: Do not generalize equal plate charges to arbitrarily precharged floating nodes, or equate a series connection with automatic voltage balancing.

independentDerivations.derivation: A noncontacting plate pair has approximately C=epsilon0*epsilon*S/d in its ideal overlap region. Winding makes large area compact without connecting the separated electrodes; in an air variable capacitor, changing S at fixed gaps changes C. Contacting the two electrode groups would instead bypass the dielectric with a conducting short.
independentDerivations.conclusion: Paper/paraffin insulation and air gaps are distinct from the foil conductors. The construction can be generalized for present-day context without deleting what the source specifically reports.

independentDerivations.derivation: At fixed effective area and dielectric permittivity, C is inversely proportional to dielectric thickness. The aluminum oxide separates foil metal from electrolyte at the operative interface. Electrolyte provides the conductive cathode there; a porous paper separator carries it and mechanically separates foils, rather than defining the very thin dielectric thickness.
independentDerivations.conclusion: The paper-as-plate source shorthand is clarified correctly. Polarity/voltage limitations are retained; the explanation does not invite handling electrolyte or a charged device.
